text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Air Zimbabwe, still smarting from expensive labour disputes and now in the process of charting a growth plan under a new chief, has lost over Z$4 million in about four months by renting two non-operational Fokker 50 aircraft.

- Chances of a partial lifting of a ban on international trade in ivory appeared to brighten yesterday following an apparent agreement on three compromise proposals by a CITES working group tasked with ironing out points on the future of the African elephant.
- A storm is brewing at the state-run Zimbabwe Broadcasting Corporation (ZBC), over plans to introduce private television on its loss-making second television channel next month.

- Indian companies have for the second year running snatched a World Bank-sponsored tender to supply Zimbabwe's government institutions with pharmaceutical products, much to the chagrin of local companies.
- A South African national has taken over as managing director of Nestle Zimbabwe, one of the country's oldest food manufacturers, which is from this month to be controlled from South Africa.

- Future ivory trade under strict conditions became more likely on Wednesday after a working group representing all of Africa at the ongoing CITES conference reached a consensus on amendments to conditions on possible resumption of the trade.
- The Commission on Global Governance meets in Harare on Friday to discuss areas of possible change in international socio-economic affairs in line with the demands of changing times.
- A Zimbabwean cabinet minister says the level of business failures in the country is too high and new entrepreneurs should go for further training in managerial skills.
